Sampling-surface test (plan 2.39.2, 60 recipes x 4 prompt surfaces built only from published text; 07_results/objective_surface.json). My registered prediction - exact overlap rises with the number of surfaces - is FALSIFIED: exact overlap at K = their neuron count is 1.67% for 1, 2, 3 and 4 surfaces alike (one recipe out of 60 at every depth). What does move is the neighbourhood: recipes with at least one of their coordinates inside our top-64 go 51.7% -> 56.7% -> 60.0% -> 60.0%, at a median rank of 11-12, and the sign agreement is 98.5-98.9% on this subset (93.4% on the full 178). So the three questions separate cleanly and should never be conflated again: the DIRECTION is reproducible (93-99%), the NEIGHBOURHOOD covers half to 60% of recipes, and the exact 1-4 coordinate LIST is not recoverable (1.67%, invariant to surfaces). The residual gap is methodological, not a sampling artefact: their coordinates are found by reading which neuron WRITES the behaviour's words in the steer lens and then validating behaviourally, whereas a first-order gradient ranks coordinates by marginal log-probability gain - and under joint/threshold effects (their own record: a 6+1 sum measured at 16, 2.3x superadditive) those are different orderings. Deliverable boundary to state publicly: we can claim positions supported by the algebra AND the three external instruments, and signs that agree with behavioural doses to 93-99%, but we must NOT claim to recover a behaviourally-searched coordinate set. Second-order probe (plan 2.39.3, 12 recipes, exact per-token Fisher in residual space where the budget metric is the identity; 07_results/objective_second_order.json). Hypothesis tested: the residual gap after 2.39.2 is the objective's CURVATURE (joint/threshold effects their recipes show, 2.3x superadditivity). Result: not confirmed - second order makes the neighbourhood WORSE, not better. Recipes with at least one of their coordinates inside our top-64: plain |g| (first order, coordinate metric) 58.3%, umag (first order, budget metric) 16.7%, second order 25.0%/16.7%/16.7% at mu=0.3/1/3. What curvature does buy is the RANK when a coordinate does appear (median 7-14 against 28 for |g|), so it narrows without widening. Exact overlap at K = their count is 0/12 here (1/60 in the 60-recipe run, so that column is noise at this sample size). Sign agreement stays 95.1% (12 recipes), consistent with 93.4% over 178 and 98.5% over 60 - direction is stable across every variant, and positions are what changes. Interpretation, now with three independent probes behind it: the community's pipeline finds SEMANTICALLY NAMEABLE coordinates (steer-lens: which neuron writes the word) and validates behaviourally, while our closed form finds the coordinates with the most effect per unit residual budget; the budget-metric correction is exactly what moves us off their picks, and that same correction is what wins +25.8% on OUR readout (2.36 K=256). Hence reproducing their coordinates is the wrong objective for our method - it would trade away our own advantage.

verdict.meaning: L14N8949 is a real, directional, dose-monotone lever that does act on the hostility readout: J2 (hostility-vs-neutral slot mass) rises +0.0059/+0.0095/+0.0191/+0.0484 over doses 0.005-0.05, positive on 6/6 held-out probes at 0.02, 8x the same-layer random control mean at 0.02 and 32x at 0.05, and the mirrored arm is negative and growing (so not a generic perturbation). What is NOT shown is exclusivity: on 3 shared contexts it never ranks first among the five hand-written trait contrasts. Two caveats keep that from being a refutation: (i) the coordinate came from one brute-force generation-based scan, i.e. a draw, not the optimum of any hostility criterion; (ii) n=3 contexts with wide per-trait spread cannot separate "not specific" from "specific but small".
verdict.S2_note: pre-registered rule not met (hostility never the max of five traits, 3/3 contexts). Power is low: 3 contexts, per-trait sd 0.011-0.044, hostility mean 0.0275 with 95% CI [-0.025, +0.080]; hostility ranks 2nd in one context (0.048 vs 0.067). So this run does not show "not hostility-specific"; it shows specificity is undemonstrated.
verdict.S2_instrument_note: The pre-registered S2 used the J1 five-trait matrix, whose five contrasts share one neutral negative; it therefore measures evaluative register, not specificity. The within-instrument test (two J2 readouts, hostile-vs-praise and praise-vs-neutral) shows the opposite of a uniform lift: h-n up, c-n down, 8/8 coordinates and dose-monotone. So S2 FAIL is an instrument result, not evidence about the coordinate.
